liebermann.notes: Usually assigned to Worcester, though Canterbury is more likely; owned by Parker, glossed and completed by Joscelin, used by Nowell and Lambarde. Contains I–II Cnut, II–III Eg, Af–Ine with Romscot and Iudex, Wulfstan's Polity and homilies, I As, I Em, III Eg again (G 2), V Atr (twice, the second G2), Grið, VIII Atr 1–5, Norðgrið, and Latin theology and canon law. Collated and copied in the 16th century in Harley 596, Jl and Bodley Junius 65.

entries.text_de:
British Museum Cotton Nero A I wird seit Wanley als sicher, wahrscheinlich oder vielleicht8 Worcester entstammend bezeichnet. Eher auf Canterbury deutet die Federprobe f. 42 Dn̄o Valtero [1313—27] D. g. āpo Cant. (doch war Walter Reynolds vorher Bischof von Worcester) und wenigstens der Text (nicht nothwendig diese Abschrift) von I Cn 3, 2; II Cn 62; Grið 8. — Parker besass den Band, Joscelin glossirte ihn und vervollständigte Lücken darin, ferner benutzten ihn Nowell und Lambard9.

f. 1 I. II Cnut, u. S. 278, von Einer Hd. um 1070, nicht ursprünglich mit Folgendem zusammenhängend, da zu Ende zwei Seiten leer sind. Um 1110 ist das Stück verbessert, im 16. Jh. mit Randnoten versehen.

f. 41—57 von Einer Hand um 1070: II. III Eg, u. S. 194; f. 45 Af-Ine, u. S. 16; mitten darin, hinter der Rubrikenliste, f. 48a Romscot und Iudex, u. S. 474 [auf f. 50b Af El 49, 9 in Quadripartitus-Übersetzung von Joscelin's Hand; auch schrieb derselbe über und neben dem Angels. Texte Glossen aus Quadrip. und Varianten aus E]; f. 51a—57b Af bis El 49, 5.

f. 58 Joscelin ergänzt Af 49, 6—Ine 54, 2 aus E.

f. 70—96, wieder von Einer Hand um 1060—80, Polity10 c. 2 ff. 11. 19. 23. 13—16. 23. 22. 17. 25. 24; Homilien11; f. 86v. I As, u. S. 146; f. 87v. (früher 88v.) I Em 1, u. S. 184. Nach jetzt fehlenden Blättern f. 88 nochmals III Eg von 3 ab, u. S. 201 als G 2 benutzt. Vgl. dg.

f. 89 V Atr, u. S. 236; f. 92v. Grið, u. S. 470; f. 95v. VIII Atr 1—5, u. S. 26312; f. 96v. Nor grið, u. S. 473. Dann zwei Blätter leer; eine Lage verloren.

f. 97—100 Eine Hand Polity 6. 1013; f. 100—5 Eine Hand, hinter ungedruckter Klage über Unsitten der Bischöfe, Polity c. 19. 13 f. 1214; f. 105v. Ostertafel 1100—15, Hand 12. Jhs., . . .

f. 109—120 Eine Hand um 1070, Polity 51; f. 110 Sermo Lupi 10142; f. 115v. Homilie3; f. 116v. nochmals V Atr, heisst S. 236: G 2; f. 120 Polity c. 1 f.4

f. 120v. Ostertafel 12. Jhs. Endet ein Theil.

f. 122v.—73 Anglolatein. Theologie, Liturgie und Kanonistisches, oft wie Hss. OP. Darin f. 127v. sog. Exc. Egberti5; f. 162v. Ps.-Theodor 49 f.6; f. 175v., Ende 11. Jhs., Gebet für König und Königin.

Der Codex ward im 16. Jh. collationirt und copirt in Harley 596, Jl und Bodley Junius 65.
entries.text_en:
British Museum Cotton Nero A I has since Wanley been described as certainly, probably or perhaps8 originating from Worcester. Pointing rather to Canterbury are the pen-trial on f. 42 Dn̄o Valtero [1313—27] D. g. āpo Cant. (though Walter Reynolds had previously been Bishop of Worcester) and at least the text (not necessarily this copy) of I Cn 3, 2; II Cn 62; Grið 8. — Parker owned the volume, Joscelin glossed it and filled gaps in it; further, Nowell and Lambarde used it9.

f. 1 I. II Cnut, below, p. 278, in one hand of c. 1070, not originally connected with what follows, since at the end two pages are blank. C. 1110 the piece was corrected, and in the 16th century provided with marginal notes.

ff. 41—57 in one hand of c. 1070: II. III Eg, below, p. 194; f. 45 Af-Ine, below, p. 16; in the middle of it, after the list of rubrics, f. 48a Romscot and Iudex, below, p. 474 [on f. 50b Af El 49, 9 in the Quadripartitus translation in Joscelin's hand; the same man also wrote above and beside the Anglo-Saxon text glosses from Quadrip. and variants from E]; ff. 51a—57b Af as far as El 49, 5.

f. 58 Joscelin supplies Af 49, 6—Ine 54, 2 from E.

ff. 70—96, again in one hand of c. 1060—80, Polity10 c. 2 ff. 11. 19. 23. 13—16. 23. 22. 17. 25. 24; homilies11; f. 86v. I As, below, p. 146; f. 87v. (formerly 88v.) I Em 1, below, p. 184. After leaves now missing, f. 88 III Eg again from 3 onward, used as G 2, below, p. 201. Cf. dg.

f. 89 V Atr, below, p. 236; f. 92v. Grið, below, p. 470; f. 95v. VIII Atr 1—5, below, p. 26312; f. 96v. Nor grið, below, p. 473. Then two leaves blank; a gathering lost.

ff. 97—100 one hand, Polity 6. 1013; ff. 100—5 one hand, after an unprinted complaint about the bad habits of the bishops, Polity c. 19. 13 f. 1214; f. 105v. Easter table 1100—15, hand of the 12th century, . . .

ff. 109—120 one hand of c. 1070, Polity 51; f. 110 Sermo Lupi 10142; f. 115v. homily3; f. 116v. V Atr again, called G 2 on p. 236; f. 120 Polity c. 1 f.4

f. 120v. Easter table, 12th century. A part ends.

ff. 122v.—73 Anglo-Latin theology, liturgy and canon law, often as in MSS OP. Therein f. 127v. the so-called Exc. Egberti5; f. 162v. Ps.-Theodor 49 f.6; f. 175v., end of the 11th century, prayer for king and queen.

The codex was collated and copied in the 16th century in Harley 596, Jl and Bodley Junius 65.

wormald.shelfmark: London, British Library, Cotton MS Nero A.i(A)
wormald.wormald_date: s. xi^med (p. 165, Table 4.1; also Ker's date, p. 224 n. 241, image checked); script points 'impartially' to either side of 1066, Wormald setting it on or just after the Conquest (pp. 224, 228)
wormald.wormald_origin: Canterbury?? (p. 165): the extra Kentish/archiepiscopal clauses in Cnut point to Canterbury, and its II–III Eg is not the Wulfstanian interpolated text, so not from a Worcester/York exemplar (p. 226). Marginal 1315 agreement involving 'Archbishop Walter' (Reynolds, earlier bishop of Worcester) (p. 226 and n. 250); 'magister Daniel de Ditone' note f. 4r (p. 225 n. 249). Leland's 'Leges aliquot regum Saxonice' at Christchurch (Hants) may be this MS (p. 228 n. 263). Known to Nowell and used for Lambarde's Archaionomia (1568) for II–III Eg; heavily glossed by Joscelyn, who completed Alfred from the Parker MS (pp. 225–6 and nn. 245–6). Talbot annotated only part B, leaving A untouched (p. 225). Joined to Nero A.i(B) probably only in the late 16th century or on entering Cotton's library (pp. 225–6).
wormald.laws: I–II Cn (divided into paragraphs with their own initials; text adjusted to Kentish law, e.g. archbishop's mundbryce, I Cn 3:2, II Cn 62); II–III Eg (non-Wulfstanian, uninterpolated text, close to Quadripartitus); Af (rubric list and Mosaic preface only, breaking off towards the end of the preface; rest supplied by Joscelyn from the Parker MS), with Romscot and Iudex inserted between Alfred's rubrics and text
wormald.laws_liebermann: I Cn, II Cn, II Eg, III Eg, Af, Ine, Romscot, Iudex, I As, I Em, V Atr, Grið, VIII Atr, Norðgrið
wormald.other_contents: Nothing but laws. Two sections in different hands: (1) Cnut, 38½ folios, followed by blank and excised leaves; (2) after an inserted blank leaf, a fresh quire with Edgar and Alfred by a second scribe (wider written space, fewer and different initials). Both sections from the same scriptorium (shared 'eft' gloss argument). Very small MS. Incomplete, and may once have held more laws or other matter (p. 228 n. 262).
wormald.overview: A small MS of about the time of the Conquest (s. xi^med), perhaps from Canterbury, containing nothing but laws: Cnut's code, Edgar's Andover code (II–III Eg) and the start of Alfred's domboc, incomplete within its preface, with the short texts Romscot and Iudex set between Alfred's rubric list and his text. Wormald argues that it had a different origin from the Wulfstan MS now bound after it (Nero A.i(B)) and that there is no sign of the two being joined until the later 1500s. Its Cnut is divided into sections, each opened by a separate initial, and adjusted to Kentish law, and its pairing of Cnut with his main sources looks forward to the twelfth-century law collections.
wormald.liebermann_superseded: Liebermann gave the whole of Nero A.i one siglum (G) as if a single MS; Wormald shows that parts A and B are separate manuscripts of different origin, not demonstrably together before the late sixteenth century, and notes that while Liebermann's 'um 1070' for part A is roughly right, his 'um 1060–80' for part B is at least forty years too late (p. 224 n. 241; pp. 225–6).
wormald.key_quote: The strongest impression left by Nero 'A' is of a patchwork with its seams showing. (p. 227)
wormald.doubts: Wormald's siglum in Table 4.1 is G, same as Liebermann's, which covers both parts. GUIDE: the guide's single entry 'G' merges parts A and B; Wormald treats Nero A.i(A) (laws only: I–II Cn, II–III Eg, Af, Romscot, Iudex) as a separate manuscript from Nero A.i(B) (Wulfstan book: Inst. Pol., homilies, I As, I Em, V Atr, Grið, VIII Atr etc.). GUIDE: 'Ine' in the guide's laws list is doubtful for this MS: Wormald says Alfred's domboc breaks off near the end of the preface (p. 226), so only the rubric list (which includes Ine's rubrics?) and part of the preface survive; Table 4.1 nonetheless writes 'Af–Ine'. Folio ranges of part A are not given by Wormald. Ker, Catalogue no. 163. Loyn's facsimile (Wulfstan Manuscript) argued for the unity of the two parts; Wormald rejects this. || Also MEL 189; 185–6 n. 97 (Wormald cross-refers to p. 225 for Nero A.i): Passing references only. Joscelyn glossed the clauses of II–III Edgar in Nero A.i (ff. 42–44v) from Harley 55, but for Cnut (ff. 3r–41r) usually followed Lambarde's printed edition. In II–III Edgar the Wulfstan manuscript G² agrees with D and Harley 55(A) against G and Quadripartitus.

verify_notes: Checked pp. 165 (image), 185–6, 189 (image: G² confirmed), 224–8 (n. 241 image: Ker 's xi med' confirmed), 232, 235, 253–4.

Overview: 'probably from Canterbury' -> 'perhaps' (Table 4.1 'Canterbury??'); 'numbered-looking paragraphs' corrected (Wormald: paragraphs with their own initials, p. 227); 'probably joined only in the later sixteenth century' rephrased to what Wormald says (p. 226).
other_contents: n. 262 says the MS is incomplete (not 'probably').

wormald.shelfmark: London, British Library, Cotton MS Nero A.i, part B (ff. 70–177)
wormald.wormald_siglum: G (Nero A.i(B)); the two texts of V Atr are G¹ (section a) and G² (section c)
wormald.wormald_date: s. xiⁱⁿ (Table 4.1, p. 164); of the archbishop's time, carrying Wulfstan's own hand, so a 'contemporary' legal manuscript (pp. 198, 202); all or most probably written after Wulfstan gave up Worcester in 1016 (p. 203); about fifty years earlier than part A (p. 198); later marginalia s. xiiiⁱⁿ, s. xiiiᵉˣ, s. xivⁱⁿ (p. 198 n. 150); twelfth-century additions on blank leaves (Table 4.2, pp. 200–1)
wormald.wormald_origin: Worcester?/York?? (Table 4.1, p. 164). The case for York is weaker than it looks: post-1016 writing, northern-interest items, later marginalia and the erasure of Wulfstan's ban on clerical marriage (f. 72v) do not prove a northern origin; best seen as made in Wulfstan's own circle wherever he was (p. 203). Sections b)–e) together by the twelfth century (p. 198); later medieval penance marginalia suggest use as a confessor's handbook (Loyn) (p. 198 n. 150); Robert Talbot's hand appears throughout (p. 202); probably joined to part A only in the late sixteenth century, possibly reduced to uniform size by Cotton's binders (pp. 198, 199, 224).
wormald.laws: Section a) (ff. 70r–96v): I As, I Em … II–III Eg (a missing bifolium has taken the text from I Em 1 to III Eg 3), V Atr (G¹), Grið, VIII Atr Pr.–5:2 only, Norðgrið (Table 4.2, p. 200; p. 203 n. 160). Section c) (ff. 109r–121v): V Atr again (G²), with Wulfstan-hand additions and corrections incl. V Atr 27, 30 (Table 4.2, p. 201; p. 199). Only the 'first', largely ecclesiastical codes of Æthelstan and Edmund, not their secular ones (p. 203).
wormald.laws_liebermann: I Cn, II Cn, II Eg, III Eg, Af, Ine, Romscot, Iudex, I As, I Em, V Atr, Grið, VIII Atr, Norðgrið
wormald.other_contents: Five sections a)–e) (Table 4.2, pp. 200–1). Old English sections a)–c): Wulfstan's Institutes of Polity (several stages of revision), Wulfstan homilies incl. the 'final' version of the 1014 Sermo Lupi (dated in this MS, rubric f. 110r), 'Admonition to Bishops', Clerical Dress; twelfth- to thirteenth-century additions (numerological lore, Easter tables, Grace, Allegory of Nebuchadnezzar, Rich and Poor, sacraments and Ten Commandments, litany, penance procedure, baptismal theory). Latin sections d)–e) (ff. 122r–177v): pre-Gregorian canon law, the Wulfstan 'Canon Collection' (Table 4.4) — De Ven. Sac., De Pastore, De Cleric. Grad., Ghaerbald's capitulary with the 'Excerptiones … Ecgberhti' rubric (f. 127v), Excerptiones de libris canonicis 1–140, 146–63 (with twelfth-century additions '141–5' on ff. 148r–149r), Pseudo-Theodore penitential, Abbo's Maundy Thursday sermon (ff. 159v–162v), Ælfric material (Fehr Anh. III–IV); these supplied Wulfstan's sources for homilies, Polity and laws (pp. 202, 213–17).
wormald.overview: The second, older part of Cotton Nero A.i is a small, pocket-sized collection of Wulfstan's writings from his own lifetime, corrected and glossed in the archbishop's own hand: homilies, the Institutes of Polity and laws (I Æthelstan, I Edmund and II–III Edgar, much of them now lost with a missing bifolium, two differing copies of V Æthelred, Grið, the opening of VIII Æthelred and Norðgrið), followed by a Latin canon-law collection that fed his Old English writings. Wormald dates it to the beginning of the eleventh century and thinks its quires may come from two or more closely similar Wulfstan MSS rather than one planned volume; it was probably joined to the later legal part A only in the sixteenth century. Its mix of law, homily and Polity suggests a moral handbook for a travelling preacher rather than a judge's manual, and its origin (Worcester or York) cannot be settled beyond Wulfstan's own circle.
wormald.liebermann_superseded: Liebermann gave both parts of Nero A.i the one siglum G and dated this part c. 1060–80 (ff. 70–96) and c. 1070 (ff. 109–20); Wormald shows it is from Wulfstan's own day (s. xiⁱⁿ, with his autograph corrections), at least forty years earlier than Liebermann thought, and probably not united with part A before the late sixteenth century (pp. 198, 224 n. 241).
wormald.pages: 198–203 (Table 4.2, pp. 200–1); 164 (Table 4.1); 197–8 (introduction to section 4); 189 (G² readings of III Eg); 213–17 and Table 4.4, pp. 214–15 (Latin sections d)–e)); 216 n. 210; 220 n. 229; 224 and n. 241
wormald.key_quote: The book or books thus look more like a vade mecum for an itinerant preacher than for a judge. (p. 203)
wormald.doubts: GUIDE: the guide's single entry G conflates parts A (ff. 3–57: I–II Cn, II–III Eg, Af–Ine, Romscot, Iudex) and B (ff. 70–177); Wormald (and Ker, nos 163/164) treat them as separate manuscripts, so the guide's laws list and dates mix both parts. GUIDE: Liebermann's dates for ff. 70–96 (c. 1060–80) and ff. 109–20 (c. 1070) are too late on Wormald's showing (s. xiⁱⁿ; ‘at least forty years too late’, p. 224 n. 241). GUIDE: the guide has ‘VIII Atr 1–5’; Table 4.1 also has ‘VIII Atr 1 – 5’, but Table 4.2 gives ‘VIII Atr Pr. – 5:2’ and n. 160 ‘only 1 – 5:2’. The guide's G2 entry calls the second text ‘in another hand (c. 1060)’: Wormald's section c) is in scribe S6 but contemporary with Wulfstan, with his corrections. Wormald's ‘[G]’ for part B is Liebermann's siglum, not a new one. The guide's note ‘usually assigned to Worcester, though Canterbury is more likely’ probably belongs to part A (Wormald gives part A ‘Canterbury??’, Table 4.1). In II–III Edgar the Wulfstan text G² agrees with D and Harley 55(A) against G and Quadripartitus (p. 189). NB the Joscelyn glosses on II–III Eg (ff. 42–44v) and Cnut (ff. 3r–41r) mentioned at p. 185 n. 97 concern part A, not this part. Marginalia dates s. xiiiⁱⁿ, s. xiiiᵉˣ, s. xivⁱⁿ checked in image (p. 198 n. 150).

origin: dropped unsourced ‘in the sixteenth century’ for Talbot.
